html: † טִפְסָר n.[m.] scribe, marshal (if meaning correct, then Assyrian loan-word, from dupsarru, tablet-writer, scribe, v. Len Langue Primit. de la Chaldée, 365 SchrCOT on Je 51:27, LotzTP 180; dupšarru, according to DlHWB 227)—pl. sf. טַפְסְרַיִךְ Na 3:17 (as if from טַפְסֵר) thy scribes, marshals, of high officials of Nineveh; abs. sg. פִּקְדוּ עָלֶיהָ טִפְסָר Je 51:27 appoint a marshal against her, i.e. against Babylon.—On military function of those skilled in writing cf. שֹׁטֵר.
